public_rationale: Marcus said newer models still seem unable to follow instructions reliably. In March 2025, Scale AI's MultiChallenge paper reported that all frontier models scored under 50% on realistic multi-turn tasks, which require accurate instruction following, and the best scored 41.4%. A July 2025 Ai2 paper found that GPT-4.1 and Claude 3.7 Sonnet, both out before the post, scored under 50% on new verifiable instructions. That paper is context only because it came out after the period. Models did score well on the simpler IFEval test, but the Ai2 authors attribute that to overfitting. On an ordinary reading of 'reliably', the evidence backs the claim.
limitations: MultiChallenge tests context use and reasoning as well as instruction following.
The in-period evidence covers models up to early 2025. Some newer models, such as o3 (April 2025), are not in the in-period source.
'Reliably' has no threshold. A reader with a looser standard might weigh the high IFEval scores more heavily.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post (May 2025), even the newest frontier language models did not follow instructions reliably. They still failed a large share of tasks on public instruction-following tests.
Marcus named no time window. I use the period from January 2025 to the post date (2025-05-12), when the frontier models he was writing about were current.

Marcus set no threshold for 'reliably'. I take an ordinary reading: failure rates near or above half on realistic instruction-following benchmarks clearly mean 'not reliable'. Near-perfect scores on hard, realistic tests would mean the opposite.
criteria.support_condition: Public benchmarks or studies from the period show frontier models of early to mid 2025 failing a substantial share of realistic instruction-following tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Public evidence from the period shows frontier models following instructions near-perfectly on hard, realistic instruction-following benchmarks, not just on saturated simple ones.

evidence.excerpt: all frontier models have less than 50% accuracy on MultiChallenge, with the top-performing Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024) achieving just a 41.4% average accuracy.
evidence.explanation: In early 2025, every frontier model tested failed more than half of realistic multi-turn tasks. The paper says these tasks need accurate instruction following. That fits 'still seems lacking'.

evidence.excerpt: All 4 challenges require accurate instruction-following, context allocation, and in-context reasoning at the same time.
evidence.explanation: Shows that the benchmark tests instruction following, though not on its own; it also tests context use and reasoning.

evidence.excerpt: we introduce IFBench with new, diverse, and challenging verifiable instruction following constraints where leading models such as GPT-4.1 or Claude 3.7 Sonnet score below 50%.
evidence.explanation: Models released before the post scored under 50% on unseen but verifiable instructions. Published after the target period, so it is context only.

evidence.excerpt: Figure 1 shows that models display good accuracy on IFEval.
evidence.explanation: Partial counterpoint: on the simpler and widely used IFEval benchmark, models already scored well. The same paper says this reflects overfitting, not general reliability.
